def04Retracted.truth: FALSE. That channel is not in the allowlist at all; the facet list deliberately excludes the base ground. All eight --ds-surface-{role} tokens ARE allowlisted and schema-accepted.

groundVsFacetLaw: The resting GROUND of a surface role is authored through --ds-surface-{role}. The --ds-material-{role}-* family carries STATES and FACETS and has no base -background by design, since the role derives it from the seed. Authoring both would be two authorities for one value.

Those compile into the vertical artifact, whose selector's second arm :where([data-ds-root][data-vertical='bithire']) matches EVERY tenant in the vertical — so they were the whole vertical's paint, unreachable by any tenant because no --ds-segmented-* token is allowlisted.

defectIntroducedAndWithdrawn.what: Authoring --ds-material-control-background-selected: #141412 delivered the black selected fill the direction wants, and made the selected segment labels INVISIBLE — black ink on a black fill.
defectIntroducedAndWithdrawn.why: The role matrix has no foreground-selected channel, so the selected label keeps resolving through --ds-material-control-foreground, which for a monochrome tenant is also ink.
defectIntroducedAndWithdrawn.decision: WITHDRAWN. Shipping an illegible selected state to gain a divergence axis is strictly worse than missing the axis. Verified legible again in capture.
defectIntroducedAndWithdrawn.blockedOn: Per the advisor the white-ink half of the inversion belongs to the emphasis leg (chrome controls / the component's selected part), NOT to a newly minted role channel. So this is blocked on that leg, not on a token request.
defectIntroducedAndWithdrawn.note: Recorded rather than quietly reverted, because the fill half DOES work and the next attempt should not rediscover the same trap.
